Senses.Explanation: The golden-winged bird is the record's great dragon-taking bird: its characteristic scene is entering or splitting the sea and seizing or swallowing a dragon. Chan masters place that recognizable scene in public questions, appraisals, teaching-seat comparisons, and reversals. Caoshan Guanghui says that Xuefeng Yicun's way of dealing with people is like the golden-winged bird entering the sea to take a dragon. Gushan Zhiyue asks what happens if the bird appears; Huanglong answers that the dragon's life will be hard to preserve, accepts that it will be swallowed, and thanks him for the offering. Yuanwu Keqin pairs the bird splitting the sea and swallowing a dragon with a lion cub leaving its cave. Hulong Taichu Qiyuan reverses the stock scene by asking why the bird-king that splits the sea and swallows a dragon is itself swallowed by a loach. When Huangbo Rong asks for the bird's straight dragon-taking, Baichi Yuan advances, makes as if to overturn the Chan seat, and leaves; Huangbo Rong recognizes him. Huangbo Yiwei An says his staff is at times the bird-king taking a dragon straightaway. Baiyun Shouduan and Ciyun Langting Jingting give two further reversals: a minute jiaoming insect swallows the bird, while the great-roc golden-winged bird's dragon-taking is called hungry indiscrimination. These are predicates, comparisons, and tests involving one creature, not different referents or an abstract quality.
Senses.Note: Exact XML count: 116 hits in 64 allowlisted texts. The bird-king form appears 50 times in 41 texts. The inherited dragon-taking lead is retained, but its phrase 'one power nothing escapes' is rejected because no stored definition or predicate establishes that universal claim. Modifier verdict: conventional-name | unresolved. The compound calls the creature 'gold-winged,' but the harvested Chan passages do not establish solid-gold construction, supply a separate color predicate, or equate gold here with enlightenment. The English 'golden-winged' retains the established name without asserting solid-gold construction or symbolism. The inherited equation with the phonetic name garuda is also not promoted: both strings occur in the allowlist, but the researched anchors do not equate them.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Mirror of the Lineage (宗鏡錄), by Yongming Yanshou. Yongming Yanshou says that as the golden-winged bird flies, a crow cannot match it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪峰和尚為人。如金翅鳥入海取龍相似。僧出問。未審和尚此間如何。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Caoshan Guanghui. Caoshan Guanghui compares Xuefeng Yicun's way of dealing with people to the golden-winged bird entering the sea to take a dragon; Caoshan Guanghui is not yet in the current roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。忽遇金翅鳥來又作麼生。龍曰。性命難存。師曰。恁麼則被他吞却去也。龍曰。謝闍黎供養。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Gushan Zhiyue. Gushan Zhiyue asks what happens if the golden-winged bird appears; the teacher recorded as Huanglong replies that the dragon's life will be hard to preserve and thanks him for the offering. Gushan Zhiyue is not yet in the current roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 等閑如金翅鳥擘海直取龍吞。似師子兒出窟妖狐絕跡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), by Yuanwu Keqin. Yuanwu Keqin pairs the golden-winged bird splitting the sea and swallowing a dragon with a lion cub leaving its cave.

Occurrences.Kwic: 金翅鳥王劈海取龍吞。因甚麼被泥鰍吞却。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Hulong Taichu Qiyuan. Hulong Taichu Qiyuan's second of three barrier-statements asks why the dragon-swallowing bird-king is swallowed by a loach; he is not yet in the current roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是金翅鳥直取龍吞？師亦進前作掀倒禪床勢而出，容遂印可。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Baichi Yuan. Huangbo Rong asks for the bird taking and swallowing a dragon; Baichi Yuan answers by advancing, making as if to overturn the Chan seat, and leaving. The headword is in Huangbo Rong's exact question, so he is the stored speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖子有時如金翅鳥王，直取龍吞；有時如摩尼寶珠，隨方顯色。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Huangbo Yiwei An. Huangbo Yiwei An says his staff is at times the golden-winged bird-king taking a dragon straightaway and at times a jewel showing color according to direction; he is not yet in the current roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 鋒刃上行，大𦦨裏走，蟭螟吞却金翅鳥。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Baiyun Shouduan (白雲守端禪師廣錄), by Baiyun Shouduan. Baiyun Shouduan reverses scale by having the minute jiaoming insect swallow the golden-winged bird.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大鵬金翅鳥，直取龍吞，也是饑不擇食。常言道：好事不如無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), section on Ciyun Langting Jingting. Ciyun Langting Jingting says the great-roc golden-winged bird taking and swallowing a dragon is hungry indiscrimination; he is not yet in the current roster.
